text:
dina: Quick sync  brought up concordia13b-int8 candidate. Big token savings but some completeness regressions on policy-synthesis and multi-step instructions. Need a one-pager for GTN/PM and routing recs.

paul: paste smoke numbers?

dina: smoke snapshot below:
```
fp16 baseline: cost_per_token = $0.0130, p95 = 172ms, baseline_accept = 0.80
int8 candidate: cost_per_token = $0.0040, p95 = 188ms, accept = 0.71
avg_tokens (synth slice) = 450
long_recall (6k) = -7.2pp, short_recall (256) = -2.0pp
hallucination_delta = +0.3pp
kv-cache hit ~79% on recent trace
```

iris: So roughly 3.25x token cost reduction. Where are failures concentrated? omissions / step-skips?

dina: Correctmostly omitted action items and missed conditional branches in step-by-step outputs. Fluency fine. Prompt-boosting recovers ~2pp.

kevin: Run hybrid (attention & norm fp16, weights int8)? Last time that helped.

dina: ran hybrid microbench: recall_long improved to -2.5pp, accept = 0.76, cost ~+24% vs pure int8 (so still ~2.3x cheaper than fp16). p95 +8ms.

canary-bot: deploy: concordia13b-int8 canary started in eu-west-1 (1 GPU). eval: https://internal/dash/models/concordia13b/canary

paul: econ quick calc (avg_tokens=450):
```
fp16_pp = 0.0130
int8_pp = 0.0040
avg_t = 450
savings_per_req = (fp16_pp - int8_pp) * avg_t = $4.05
```

iris: $4 saved per request is material. But if a 7.2pp recall drop reduces retention or conversion on those flows, could be net negative. Need product LTV sensitivity.

kevin: Proposed traffic plan: default hybrid for synthesis/long outputs; int8 for ephemeral/drafts and high-throughput background jobs; fp16 pinned for flagged "final" outputs and top-tier customers. Use intent-based routing + token-estimate heuristic.

dina: Will assemble a short scorecard: [variant, cost_per_token, p95_latency, recall_long_pp, recall_short_pp, hallucination_pp, accept_delta_pp, recommended_route, rollout_gates].

paul: Rollout gates: require recall_long >= -4pp AND accept_drop <= 3pp on 24h rolling window. Also block if hallucination increases >1pp. Auto-rollback if accept_drop >4pp in 12h.

canary-bot: eval job complete (400 samples) -> https://internal/evals/concordia13b/400

dina: short summary from 400-sample eval: int8 long_recall = -6.9pp, hallucination +0.4pp, accept_drop = 4.1pp. hybrid long_recall = -2.3pp, hallucination +0.2pp, accept_drop = 1.2pp.

iris: Looks like hybrid is the pragmatic compromise. We should include priming sensitivity and a small prompt tweak matrix in the scorecard; some failures fixed by a 1-line priming tweak.

kevin: Ops ask: add rolling flagged-slice eval and an automatic canary rollback if accept_drop >3pp over 6h for flagged slices (policy-synthesis, legal-summaries).

paul: I'll prepare a short cost-sim table for monthly volumes and LTV break-even points for GTN. Example row: monthly_summaries=50k -> gross_savings = 50k * $4.05 = $202.5k; show revenue loss scenarios.

dina: created ticket INF-3001 linking canary, eval CSV, and scorecard. Uploading sample failures and prompt beta tweaks.

iris: Recommend 2k-sample A/B on production-labeled slices before any >20% traffic reallocation. 400-sample still noisy.

kevin: If GTN wants faster decision, propose staged soft-roll: hybrid to 25% of synthesis traffic, fp16 pinned for final exports, int8 for drafts. Monitor conversion proxy and acceptability closely for 7 days.

dina: will post scorecard + simple routing rules and soft-roll plan. Tagging PMs and GTN. :spiral_notepad:

paul: LGTM. Ping me when scorecard is live; I'll finalize routing flags and the sim table.

(canary note: evals are small-sample; larger A/B required to be decisive)
